Courtesy of Kaia's Island Kitchen and Tiki Bar
Hawaiian Restaurant and Tiki Bar Coming to Danville
Danville’s Vine and Spirits is trading in earthy cabernet for island breezes. The casual wine bar annex to Bridges Restaurant and Bar is shuttered temporarily, but plans to reopen in early April as Kaia’s Island Kitchen and Tiki Bar . According to owner Randy Negi —a longtime owner of Bridges who sold the restaurant last year but retained the Vine—Kaia’s will be more of a food-forward concept with a full menu of Hawaiian-influenced fare. That will include entrées such as Kahlua pork, loco moco, macadamia-nut-encrusted mahi mahi, and miso salmon. There will be a “bowl” section that includes poke and several salads, while the lunch menu will offer a “mixed plate”: a famed affordable lunch option in Hawaii that consists of two scoops of rice, macaroni salad, and a choice of protein. Negi, who is of Japanese descent, says he’s always enjoyed Hawaii’s melting pot of Asian cuisine and saw it as filling a void in the Danville dining scene.
“I’ve traveled quite a bit to Hawaii and always loved the food there: It’s essentially my favorite thing to eat,” he says. “Danville has a lot of Italian and pizza, and I wanted to bring something different.”
While Negi is particularly excited about the food, he admits that it’s the tiki component that’s generating the most buzz.
“I definitely want this to be a restaurant first,” he says. “But when I try to tell people that I’m opening this island restaurant, everyone asks me: ‘Hey, I hear you’re opening a tiki bar?’”
Which is also true: the bar program at Kaia’s will indeed feature classic tiki drinks—mai tais, zombies, and the like—served in themed glassware including custom mugs made especially for the restaurant. And it turns out that Negi has some inside help on that front: Head brewer Matt Sager at Danville Brewing Company (where Negi is a partner) happens to be a “tiki fanatic” and took the lead in putting together the cocktail menu.
That being said, the interior will have more of a lighter, Hawaiian-island feel than a tiki-heavy theme. Negi hopes to launch Kaia’s during the second week of April, when it will be open for dinner to start, followed by lunch and weekend brunch service.
Fun Drinking Options Abound
Courtesy of the Syndicate
Indeed, the tiki spirit seems to be alive and well in the suburban East Bay. The Boo Loo Lounge has been a hit since launching in late 2023 in downtown Orinda, while Tiki Tom’s is going strong in Walnut Creek. In Livermore, Nightcaps at Rosetta , the newly started evening-time dessert and cocktail spin-off from the owners of Rosetta Roasting coffee shop, hosts periodic tiki takeover nights. Meanwhile the Fat Pigeon , a cocktail bar that changes themes and drinks every few months, just debuted its newest pop-up motif: Alice in Wonderland. Creative concoctions include the Queen of Hearts, a red mango-infused Moscow mule; the Looking Glass, a fruity clarified milk punch; and the savory gin fizz Metamorphosis.
And after weeks of teasing via social media, the Last Word is back up and running with a new name and concept in downtown Livermore. While ownership and management remains the same, the Syndicate sports a refreshed interior with a 1oungy, 1920s-1940s speakeasy vibe complete with velvet couches, amber lighting, and cocktails named after famous Prohibition-era gangsters, including Al Capone, Lucky Luciano, and Bonnie and Clyde (pineapple-and-lavender-infused pisco with lime and passion fruit topped with hot white chocolate cream). The bar carries over 400 spirits, while food offerings are anchored by elevated sandwiches, such as a lobster roll and gochujang-glazed Korean fried chicken sandwich.
Daytrip Embraces Chicken
Welcome news comes courtesy of the San Francisco Chronicle : Oakland’s lauded (then shuttered) Daytrip is indeed reopening with a new casual, chicken-centric concept. The nationally acclaimed Temescal sit-down dinner destination closed last year citing an unsustainable business model. However owners Finn Stern and Stella Dennig regrouped and will launch Daytrip Counter later this month with counter service and a menu centered on rotisserie chicken. Available in half and whole portions, as well as in salads and sandwiches, the aggressively seasoned chicken is brined overnight and injected with a chicken fat and stock sauce while roasting for maximal flavor. Yum.

Veteran Danville restaurateur Randy Negi (longtime owner of Bridges and a partner at Danville Brewing Company) built the concept around family trips to Hawaii and named it for his granddaughter Kaia, whose painted portrait greets guests near the entrance. The menu is food-first Hawaiian comfort fare — Spam musubi, poke crisps and bowls, loco moco, chicken katsu, kalbi beef, macadamia-crusted catch and a shareable Hula Pie — paired with a serious tiki program (a '44 Mai Tai, Ohanapod Mai Tai, Chi Chi, Zombie, Navy Grog, rum flights) assembled with help from Danville Brewing head brewer Matt Sager. The room mixes bamboo, thatch, carved tiki statues, blown-glass orbs, a sunset beach mural and colorful lighting, with an island garden patio (heaters and tiki torches), a reservable "Celi's Beach Hut," daily brunch and lunch, a keiki menu, and live Hawaiian music on Fridays.
